newsitem.title: POLAND: Slaski plans to invest in retail growth.
newsitem.headline: Slaski plans to invest in retail growth.

text.p: Poland's Bank Slaski SA, a subsidiary of the ING Bank NV, plans to spend at least $100 million over the next three years on the expansion of retail banking , Slaski's chief executive said on Wednesday.
Brunon Bartkiewicz told a news conference the bank. 54-percent owned by the ING, wanted to increase its share of the retail banking market to 10 percent from the current six percent. @

"In the next three years our spending on the development of the retail banking will reach several hundred million dollars," Bartkiewicz said at a joint conference of financial institutions from the ING Group.
"We would like to have a significant position on this market which means about a 10 percent (share)," Bartkiewicz said.
He added that Slaski should be able to finance the expansion from its profits without having to raise capital through new share issues. @

"We are capable of financing such investments from our profits and we can create additional value for our shareholders...so we do not envisage raising capital through new share issues," Bartkiewicz said.

He said that Slaski planned to spend about $20 million on several operating centres dealing with such areas as credit cards, cheques, consumer loans. Another $10 million would cost the overhaul of the bank's telecommunications system.
Bartkiewicz said the most costly part of the expansion would be the construction of new branch offices. @
Slaski now has 112 full service branches and service outlets. -- Robert Bogdanski +48 22 653 9700
